decision: PERVASIVENESS_ESTABLISHED_UNIDIMENSIONALITY_OPEN: 'one global self-evaluation quantity' is an over-claim relative to this covariance structure; corrected to 'non-selective self-evaluation movement' in REPORT.md.
decision_rule: A 'single quantity' claim requires the per-item effect fluctuations to share one factor (uniformly positive, high pairwise correlations). Heterogeneous or negative correlations refute the strong reading at tested power.
notes: Correction prompted by external research feedback 2026-08-15. Underpowered by design (10 families); a proper test needs more families or item-pair replication within family.

values.floor_note: the two non-movers (distress, unpleasantness) sit at the 0-rail with no downward-relevant headroom; 'everything moves' is properly 'every self-directed item WITH HEADROOM moves'
values.method: Per-family SELF-FAIL minus SELF-SUCC effect series (10 families) for all 9 SCALE items across the main and B batteries; pairwise Pearson correlation of the demeaned family fluctuations among the 7 items whose |mean effect| > 0.05.
values.question: Is the self-attribution-gated movement ONE latent quantity, as 'global self-evaluation shift' could be read to assert?
values.reading: Pervasiveness across self-directed items is established (7/7 headroom items move, trait items most). UNIDIMENSIONALITY IS NOT: the family-fluctuation correlation structure is heterogeneous (mean +0.23, range -0.78..+0.89), inconsistent with a single latent driving all items, though n=10 families gives little power and per-family fluctuations are noise-dominated for small-effect items. The defensible claim: NON-SELECTIVE self-evaluation movement, magnitude ordered by the item's evidential relevance to task failure (capacity > mood > floor-pinned valence); whether it is one variable or several is OPEN.
